problem: The Navigation from Dialogue History (NDH) task on CVDN cuts each dialogue into sub-path instances, so the agent lacks supervision toward the final goal region. Its primary metric, Goal Progress (GP), rewards wandering near the goal without following the instructed path.
motivation: Instruction-following navigation should be judged on path fidelity, not just on getting close to the goal. The authors trained the same model with a global-target reward and a local-target reward. The global-target model had higher GP but much lower SR and nDTW and a much longer trajectory, so GP and fidelity conflict under the sub-path setup.
key_idea: Merge the sub-path NDH instances into one full path with its full dialogue (NDH-Full), giving full supervision toward the goal and using nDTW as the main metric, and provide a baseline with a dialogue progressor module.
insight: Table 3 shows that the global-target reward gives higher GP (5.51 vs 3.82) but lower SR (19.8 vs 37.2), lower nDTW (0.253 vs 0.518) and a much longer TL (24.6 vs 10.6). So agents raise GP by wandering, and GP is a poor measure of instruction following. On NDH-Full, full dialogue beats the no-dialogue and target-only baselines in every metric, but the gaps are small. Curriculum learning, pre-training and speaker-based data augmentation give no clear gain, so the task remains hard.
method: NDH-Full task construction: combine the NDH sub-paths of the same CVDN dialogue into one full path and full dialogue, keeping the sub-path/dialogue-round alignment; 1145/260/248 train/val-unseen/test-unseen instances, no val-seen split.
LXMERT-based navigation model: ResNet panoramic features and a dialogue transformer feed cross-modal transformer layers. Next-view logits come from attention scores over candidate views.
Visual proxy token: links the candidate views to the view history and serves as the recurrent state. It is passed through a linear layer to the next step.

Dialogue progressor (NDH-Full): compares scores from [proxy token; current-round first-token feature] against those for the next round, using the current visual observation to decide whether to advance the dialogue round. It is trained from the sub-path/round alignment.
Pre-training for NDH: an objective close to the main navigation task (next view selection plus masked view and masked language modeling) on CVDN, R2R and part of the R2R augmented data.
Training: mixed IL and RL (Actor-Critic) with LMIX=LIL+λLRL. The reward is distance-to-goal for NDH and nDTW for NDH-Full. NDH-Full uses CLIP (ResNet50) visual features.
Explored enhancements: curriculum learning over the number of dialogue rounds, pre-trained weights, and speaker-model-generated oracle instructions as augmentation.

setting.backbone: LXMERT-style vision-language transformer (9 language / 5 cross-modal layers, trained from scratch, not the LXMERT weights) with ResNet-152 or CLIP-ResNet50 features
setting.training_data: NDH: pre-training on CVDN, R2R and part of the R2R augmented data, then fine-tuning on CVDN only. NDH-Full: trained on the 1145 NDH-Full training instances without pre-training.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views (ResNet / CLIP features) plus dialogue text
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (selection among candidate views)

numbers_note: Table 2 (NDH GP) is listed under CVDN, since NDH is built on it and has no canonical benchmark name. Other rows (Table 3 reward analysis, curriculum learning, data augmentation, baselines) are omitted or are not the main method.
results: On NDH the model reaches GP 5.27 on test-unseen, the top of the leaderboard at the time, above BabyWalk (4.46) and EAML (3.91). On NDH-Full the Full-Dialogue model beats Random-Walk, No-Dialogue and Target-Only in all metrics (val-unseen SR 7.7, nDTW 0.277), but absolute scores are low.
limitations: Baseline gains on NDH-Full are small and the absolute SR is low, and none of the tried enhancements (curriculum learning, pre-training, augmentation) clearly helps.
NDH-Full is small (1653 instances) and has no val-seen split.
The speaker-model augmentation is of insufficient quality for long paths.
